name: Ikram Aliskerov
event: UFC Fight Night: Procházka vs. Stirling
summary: A Dagestani middleweight (18-2; 5-1 UFC; age 34 in our data) and combat sambo world champion (Cageside) out of KHK MMA. His only losses are first-round knockouts to Khamzat Chimaev (Brave, 2019) and Robert Whittaker (2024, a short-notice main event in only his third UFC fight). He has won three straight since, the last two by wrestling-heavy 30-27 decisions over Jun Yong Park and Brunno Ferreira.

how_they_fight.Striking: Accurate and powerful: about 5.2 significant strikes a minute at 57%, 0.65 knockdowns per 15, and seven KO/TKO wins (three in the UFC, all in R1: Hawes, Alves, Muniz). Uses a jab, leg kicks, teeps and straight punches; landed a knee before his R1 takedown of Ferreira and met Ferreira's R3 rush with straight shots (Cageside).
how_they_fight.Grappling: His base. About 3.3 takedowns per 15 at 59%. Our data has him at 5 of 7 takedowns and 367 seconds of control against Park, and 5 of 6 with 533 seconds against Ferreira. He took Ferreira down in every round and threatened several submissions (Cageside, LowKick), and ended the Park fight on the back with a body triangle. Five career submission wins. Cageside noted he couldn't hold Park down after early takedowns and 'didn't do much on top' in R2.
how_they_fight.Defense: Solid takedown defense (about 72%). His defensive hole is on the feet against elite strikers: both losses were R1 knockouts by strikes (Chimaev 2:26, Whittaker 1:49). Our data has Whittaker out-landing him 14-5 before the finish. Absorbs about 3.7 a minute.
how_they_fight.Pace & cardio: A fast starter who can also grind. Twelve stoppage wins: eight in R1, one in R2, three in R3 (all pre-UFC). His last two fights went the full 15 minutes with takedowns late, including a key R3 takedown under Park's pressure (Cageside), so he hasn't faded. Both losses came early in R1. Said after the Park fight that he never gets tired in three-round sparring and that his plan was to feel Park out rather than pressure him; his corner wasn't happy with how cautious it was (Cageside).
how_they_fight.Fight IQ: Disciplined and game-plan driven; takes the low-risk route once ahead. Called for a top opponent after Baku (Cageside).

patterns: Takedowns in every round, long top control and back takes
R1 finisher before the UFC and early in his UFC run; grinding decisions lately

concerns: Chin against a big puncher early in R1

keys_to_beat: Hurt him early: both losses came inside the first 2:30
Defend the first takedown and get up fast; make him work for every reset
Pressure him and make him uncomfortable, as Park did

news.text: Booked against Jared Cannonier for the Qatar card; Wikipedia lists it on the main card.
Beat Brunno Ferreira by unanimous decision (30-27 x3) for his third straight win; called for a top opponent afterwards.
